newsitem.title: GERMANY: German oilseeds area estimate revised downward.
newsitem.headline: German oilseeds area estimate revised downward.

text.p: Germany's 1997 oilseeds area estimate for both food and non-food use has been reduced to 949,912 hectares from June figures, but it is still above the area last year, farm price and marketing office ZMP said.
The comparable area last year, which included winter and spring rapeseed and sunflowerseed, totalled 897,383 ha.
A weekly report from ZMP detailed the figures, citing extensive surveys carried out by statistics offices in the individual German states, which included responses up to July 15.
The figures imply Germany would be in line with oilseeds area limits for food use under an international trade accord.
The new total was down from a 1,021,689 ha forecast obtained from statistics office and regional chambers of agriculture in June, which was based on a smaller poll and data up to April.
The latest total was broken down as follows -- winter rapeseed 859,025 ha (777,190 ha in the 1996 harvest), spring rapeseed 56,988 ha (76,435) and sunseed 33,899 ha (43,758).
ZMP did not give a breakdown for food and non-food areas but the final non-food registration figure published last month by state intervention board BLE was 112,584 ha.

Deducted from the 949,912 ha total, this would result in a German food area of 837,328 -- almost precisely in line with the 836,099 ha limit allocated to Germany for food use under the European Union/United States Blair House accord.
A private survey issued by oilseeds lobby UFOP in February had put food plantings for the 1997 harvest at just 740,640 ha.
